claims.text: Colonial land dispossession reduced access to productive resources in Namibia. Contract labour and migrant work could separate wage earners from rural households, increasing the farming and caring tasks left to women. Discriminatory access to education and formal jobs restricted some women’s alternatives, while cash-crop and wage relationships changed how households met needs. Do not describe women as passive or all households as identical: women also produced food, traded, organised and adapted to these pressures. Judge control of land and income as well as labour performed; a heavier contribution need not bring stronger decision rights.
